<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919413_theRebbe_617" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919413_theRebbe_617__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The recitation of song comes specifically through the journeys of the Jewish people, paralleling how the entire service of Torah and mitzvos requires movement, and this pattern of descent for the sake of ascent applies to the future redemption as well.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the recitation of the aforementioned song comes about through the journeys of the children of Israel</t>
    <t s="2">(as it is written before this: "From there they journeyed and encamped on the other side of Arnon... therefore it is said..."36).</t>
    <t s="3">And this is similar to how the entire matter of Torah and mitzvos comes specifically through travel,</t>
    <t s="4">as is stated regarding the Giving of the Torah:37</t>
    <t s="5">"And Hashem descended upon Mount Sinai"</t>
    <t s="6">(the journey of the Holy One, blessed be He),</t>
    <t s="7">and "To Moshe He said, 'Ascend to Hashem'"</t>
    <t s="8">(the journey of the children of Israel).</t>
    <t s="9">So too is it in the service of every single Jew, that the beginning of service is "Go for yourself from your land, from your birthplace, and from your father's house" — the departure from one's nature, habit, and coarseness</t>
    <t s="10">(as is explained in the continuation of the year 5666,38</t>
    <t s="11">the details of the matters of "your land," "your birthplace," and "your father's house"),</t>
    <t s="12">and specifically through this, "I will bless you, magnify your name, and you will be a blessing," until "all the families of the earth will be blessed through you."</t>
    <t s="13">So too is it regarding the revelation of the future redemption,</t>
    <t s="14">that then the matter of "all the families of the earth will be blessed through you" will be in revelation and in ultimate perfection, as it is stated:39</t>
    <t s="15">"Then I will turn to the nations a clear language, to call all of them in the name of Hashem, to serve Him with one accord,"</t>
    <t s="16">that the revelation of the future redemption comes specifically through the preceding exile.40</t>
    <t s="17">And analogous to the song "Spring up, O well..."</t>
    <t s="18">(at the beginning of the entry into the land)</t>
    <t s="19">which came specifically through the matter of journeys, as above,</t>
    <t s="20">similarly is it also regarding the song of "Sing to Hashem a new song"</t>
    <t s="21">[<a href="/library/bible_cdo/aid/2006154#v312" data-book-id="11380-2006154" title="Tehillim 96,</t>
    <t s="22">which is" target="_blank">Tehillim 96,</t>
    <t s="23">which is the chapter of the Baal HaGeulah that was begun on 12 Tammuz41],</t>
    <t s="24">which refers to the song of the future redemption</t>
    <t s="25">[therefore it is stated "a new song" in the masculine form,</t>
    <t s="26">because the future redemption is a complete and eternal redemption after which there is no exile42],</t>
    <t s="27">that this comes specifically through the preceding exile.</t>
    <t s="28">For the matter of exile is</t>
    <t s="29">(similar to the letter vav)</t>
    <t s="30">derived from the matter of "And He drove him out" through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge,43</t>
    <t s="31">and before that, the matter of the diminution of the moon,44</t>
    <t s="32">which descent was with deliberate intent</t>
    <t s="33">(as the Mitteler Rebbe45 explains</t>
    <t s="34">at length regarding the matter of "He who works wonders with the children of men"46)</t>
    <t s="35">so that through the descent there would subsequently be the ultimate ascent and perfection in Israel,</t>
    <t s="36">through which there will be, automatically, the ultimate ascent and perfection in the entire order of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="37">beginning from this lowest world, beneath which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="38">as per the analogy of the lever:47</t>
    <t s="39">when one wishes to lift a house or the like with it,</t>
    <t s="40">one must grasp the lever at the lowest part of the house,</t>
    <t s="41">and specifically through the lifting of the lowest part, the entire house is lifted.</t>
    <t s="42">In a similar manner is it also regarding the ascent of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="43">that specifically through the ascent of this lowest world, an ascent is made in all the worlds,</t>
    <t s="44">and an ascent in an incomparable manner,</t>
    <t s="45">as explained in the continuation of the day of the Hilula48</t>
    <t s="46">(of the Baal HaGeulah),</t>
    <t s="47">that the matter of "below without end" is connected to the matter of "above without limit."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The statement of the Baal HaGeulah that only the body went into exile, not the soul, is understood through the concept that since the exile is by Divine command, the service of Torah and mitzvos during exile has an eternal quality, and through contemplating that the descent is for the sake of ascent, even the animal soul can be at rest.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">Based on the above, the statement of the Baal HaGeulah49 will be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">that only the body went into exile, not the soul.</t>
    <t s="3">For at first glance, it is stated in the Gemara50</t>
    <t s="4">that exile confuses understanding and comprehension,</t>
    <t s="5">and certainly comprehension and understanding in the manner of arriving at the halachic conclusion,</t>
    <t s="6">so apparently exile also affects the souls.</t>
    <t s="7">However, one explanation of this</t>
    <t s="8">is based on what is stated in Tractate Eruvin:51</t>
    <t s="9">"Since it is written of them, 'By the word of Hashem they encamped, and by the word of Hashem they journeyed,' it is considered as if they are permanently settled,"</t>
    <t s="10">that since the encampment is by the word of Hashem,</t>
    <t s="11">therefore</t>
    <t s="12">(even though it is only temporary)</t>
    <t s="13">it is considered significant enough to be deemed permanent.</t>
    <t s="14">For similarly is it also regarding the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="15">since it is by the word of Hashem,52</t>
    <t s="16">therefore the service of Torah and mitzvos53</t>
    <t s="17">during the time of exile is in a manner of permanence and eternity.</t>
    <t s="18">And this matter is not a mere decree, but can also be explained in the intellect of the G-dly soul based on what is explained in Tanya,54</t>
    <t s="19">that the unification achieved through the study of Torah and the fulfillment of mitzvos is eternal forever and ever,</t>
    <t s="20">and this eternal unification</t>
    <t s="21">(which is above)</t>
    <t s="22">is also below.55</t>
    <t s="23">And this matter can also be explained in the intellect of the animal soul</t>
    <t s="24">[that the purpose of Torah study is that through the intellect of the G-dly soul,</t>
    <t s="25">the intellect of the animal soul will also be unified in a wondrous unification,56</t>
    <t s="26">etc.],</t>
    <t s="27">that since57</t>
    <t s="28">the supernal intent in the descent is for the sake of ascent,</t>
    <t s="29">it is simple that the One who brought about the descent is the Master both of the descent and of the ascent,58</t>
    <t s="30">and it is understood that the matter of "descent for the sake of ascent" is in ultimate perfection,</t>
    <t s="31">meaning that every detail in the descent is only for the sake of the ascent.</t>
    <t s="32">And since He, blessed be He, is the Essence of good, and it is the nature of the good to do good,</t>
    <t s="33">to the point that we use the term "nature" regarding this, so to speak,59</t>
    <t s="34">it is therefore understood that His choice of such a great descent is because this is the only path through which it is possible to arrive at this great ascent.</t>
    <t s="35">And through this contemplation, one also affects the animal soul so that it is at rest,</t>
    <t s="36">and then not only is the G-dly soul not in exile, but even the animal soul is not in exile,</t>
    <t s="37">for even the powers of the animal soul</t>
    <t s="38">(including the power of intellect)</t>
    <t s="39">are in their ultimate perfection,</t>
    <t s="40">from which perspective one can have understanding and comprehension in Torah, even to the point of arriving at the halachic conclusion</t>
    <t s="41">(even during the time of exile),</t>
    <t s="42">because even from the perspective of his animal soul, he is in a state of rest.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Even if one has not yet internalized the concept that the descent is only for the sake of ascent, by desiring and yearning to be on the level of ascent, one is already there through thought, and the advice for overcoming external distractions is to pray with "heaviness of head," which reveals this thought.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, even when one has not reached the aforementioned level,</t>
    <t s="2">because the above reasoning — that the descent into this lowest world, beneath which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="3">and especially the descent of the footsteps of Mashiach</t>
    <t s="4">(within the low world itself)</t>
    <t s="5">which is a very great descent, as explained in the Talmud60</t>
    <t s="6">and as we also see empirically with physical eyes,</t>
    <t s="7">is only for the sake of ascent, and therefore it is not a true descent61 — has not yet been absorbed in his intellect,</t>
    <t s="8">nevertheless, since he desires and yearns to be on the level of ascent,</t>
    <t s="9">through this very fact he is on that level,</t>
    <t s="10">as per the statement of the Baal Shem Tov:62</t>
    <t s="11">"Where a person's thought and will are, there he is."</t>
    <t s="12">However, since there are external matters that confuse and conceal,</t>
    <t s="13">the advice for this is: "One should not stand to pray except out of heaviness of head."63</t>
    <t s="14">Prayer is the matter of connection</t>
    <t s="15">[for this is what they said: "Would that a person pray all day long,"64</t>
    <t s="16">meaning that the entire day should be in such connection as during prayer,</t>
    <t s="17">know65</t>
    <t s="18">before Whom you stand],</t>
    <t s="19">and the preparation is the matter of "heaviness of head,"</t>
    <t s="20">for through the heaviness of head, the distracting matters are nullified.</t>
    <t s="21">And especially according to the teaching of the Maggid,66</t>
    <t s="22">that the intent of "heaviness of head" is the heaviness of the "Head of all heads," and this feeling comes through the contemplation that the soul is "a part of G-d from above"</t>
    <t s="23">[In the teaching of the Maggid there, the phrase "a part of G-d from above" is quoted,67</t>
    <t s="24">without adding the word "literally."</t>
    <t s="25">And in this we see the innovation of the Alter Rebbe in the Tanya,68</t>
    <t s="26">which is the Written Torah of Chabad Chassidus69],</t>
    <t s="27">through this, all matters that obscure and conceal are nullified,</t>
    <t s="28">and immediately his thought is revealed</t>
    <t s="29">[that there he is,</t>
    <t s="30">as above],</t>
    <t s="31">that from the perspective of his thought, he is in the level of ascent.</t>
    <t s="32">And from the level of thought,</t>
    <t s="33">the essence of which thought is at the level of the soul that is above time and space,</t>
    <t s="34">for this thought is the very essence of the person, as it is stated in the Tikunei Zohar:70</t>
    <t s="35">"What is 'man'? Thought. He thought 'what'... that he is 'man' [meaning] thought,"</t>
    <t s="36">from this level of the soul that is above time and space, it is subsequently drawn down also into his intellect,</t>
    <t s="37">so that even in his intellect, the reasoning is absorbed that since "by the word of Hashem they encamped," it is considered as if they are permanently settled,</t>
    <t s="38">and this is subsequently drawn down also into actual deed.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
